**Stacked on #345663** (Block 1, workbench parts foundation). Review only the commits after `3ecd7cb59d4` (#345663's head, on main `dd554ae2e6b`). Draft until #345663 merges; it then rebases onto main.

Block 2 of the chat windows parts design: chat windows of the Agents window built on parts. It supersedes #344666 (F1) at the parity gate, and carries the sessions half of #345076 and the wallpaper half of #345561.

## What changes

- **Chat windows live in `vs/workbench/contrib/chatWindow`.**
  - `IChatWindowService` opens a chat in a window of its own, with a chat part beside a main part. Both are `ContentPart`s on the window's `PartGrid`.
  - `IChatWindowProvider` supplies the content, chrome, look and move-back facets. There are no chat window kinds.
  - The window covers layout modes, per-chat sizes and layouts, restore after reload, Move to Main Window, and moving the chat editor out of its window (Q9).
- **The Agents window is the only provider (`vs/sessions`).**
  - `'sessions.chat'` is a view editor over `SessionView`. It brings its own title, and input-only works through its size constraints.
  - The provider supplies the title row and strip, the cards and wallpaper, and the per-window session keys.
  - The entry points are behind `sessions.chatWindows.enabled`.
- **Generic per-window keys:** `layoutMode`, `splitLayout`, `terminalsVisible` and `terminalsPosition`. They are bound per window and unset elsewhere. There are no chat-window-only keys, flags or parameters.
- **Terminals:** they open in a part-grid cell, and the terminal position moves that cell. Terminal links open in the window's main part.
- **Changes editor:** it is the same in every window. Each changeset operation is registered once and acts on the invoking editor's session. The changed-files list comes from #345658 (merged in main); chat windows turn it on.
- **Platform API restored: `INativeHostService.handleTitleDoubleClick`** (removed in 402f07b34ce as unused). A double-click on the empty space of a tab row at the top edge of a chat window (which shares the title bar) now does what a title-bar double-click does: macOS follows `AppleActionOnDoubleClick` (zoom / minimize / none), Windows and Linux maximize or restore. The double-click reaches the renderer there, so it is routed in the renderer instead of opening an untitled editor. Generic, in `native.ts`, `nativeHostMainService`, `IBaseWindow`/`BaseWindow`; please review.
- **Generic part grid markers:** next to the top-edge markers, `PART_GRID_RIGHT_EDGE_CLASS` (cells) and `PART_GRID_TOP_RIGHT_GROUP_CLASS` (the group at the top right). In Side by Side on Windows/Linux, the top-right tab row keeps the room of the window controls that float above it.
- **Base fix found here:** `GridView.maximumWidth` returned the maximum height. #345663 carries the fix, and it is also coming as its own main PR.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Title-bar double-click (`INativeHostService.handleTitleDoubleClick`, restored):** a double-click on the empty space of a tab row at the top edge of a chat window is routed to the title bar's action only when it reaches the renderer. Where the OS takes that space as the window's caption (Chromium's drag region: the native caption on Windows and Linux, the drag area on macOS), the OS handles the double-click itself (maximize/restore, or zoom/minimize per `AppleActionOnDoubleClick`) and the page never sees the event, so only one of them acts on every platform. With the native title bar the routing is off, as the tab rows are not at the window's top then.
- **Side-panel key and terminals:** `workbench.action.agentToggleSidePanel` is now in the terminal's skip-shell list, so its key toggles the side panel (or a chat window's editor) instead of being sent to the shell, also in the main window's terminals, like the other Agents layout keys there.
- **Unarchive with an argument:** the Unarchive action acts on the session its argument names (the Changes toolbar of a chat window names that window's session). Without an argument it acts on the active session, as before. An argument that names no shown session does nothing, rather than unarchiving the active session.
- **Session actions from a chat window:** a session resource given to an action resolves to the session of the focused chat window when that window shows it, before the main window's wrapper of the same session. Extension commands of the Changes toolbar keep receiving the resource.

Regular VS Code is unchanged: nothing registers a provider, and the contribution loads only in the Agents window.

## How to test

Turn on `sessions.chatWindows.enabled` in the Agents window, then use Open Chat in New Window. With Playwright, stub `document.hasFocus = () => false` in the windows that aren't in front: CDP focus emulation makes every window look focused.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous double-layout call chain is explicit in the grid and terminal implementations, and width-only window resizing guarantees cases where the corrective resize is redundant. Exact frame cost varies with pane content and hardware.
Findings.PerformanceResource: full part-grid, editor-pane, and xterm layout CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The duplicate work runs for every auxiliary-window resize event while terminals are visible, and scales with the number and complexity of cells/editor panes in that chat window.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased main-thread resize latency and dropped frames, with redundant terminal dimension evaluation and possible coalesced PTY resize work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Without the new chat-window grid path, resizing did not perform this extra post-layout `resizeCell` pass to preserve a chat-window terminal height.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After `grid.layout(width, height)` has already laid out every visible cell, the added branch always calls `_resizeTerminals`, even when the terminal height is unchanged (for example during width-only resizing). `resizeCell` unconditionally enters `Grid.resizeView`/`SplitView.resizeView`, whose relayout lays out the grid and active terminal editor again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 342 performs `_resizeTerminals(grid, terminalsHeight)` after every noninitial layout whenever the terminal cell is visible, without checking whether `grid.layout` changed its height.
Findings.Title: Avoid the unconditional second grid layout on resize
Findings.Impact: Dragging the edge of a chat window with terminals open performs two full layout passes per resize event; TerminalEditor then invokes TerminalInstance.layout again, making interactive resizing visibly more prone to jank.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 337-342 capture the terminal height, call `grid.layout`, then unconditionally call `_resizeTerminals`; that helper reads the current width and calls `PartGrid.resizeCell`. `PartGrid.resizeCell` delegates to `Grid.resizeView`, and `SplitView.resizeView` always calls `relayout`. TerminalEditor.layout calls `instance.layout`, which reevaluates rows/columns and schedules process dimensions. The same file's `_update` path already demonstrates the bounded guard by comparing the post-layout height before resizing at lines 391-392.
Findings.Recommendation: At minimum, mirror the existing `_update` guard and call `_resizeTerminals` only when the post-layout terminal height differs; ideally feed the preserved terminal height into a single grid layout transaction so height-changing resizes also avoid laying out terminal/editor content twice.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path from repeated toggle/show calls to asynchronous terminal creation is explicit, and terminal visibility cannot flip until after the awaited launch and editor move. The only uncertainty is how often users overlap requests; slow remote terminal startup makes the trigger realistic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: terminal subprocesses and their renderer/process objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost grows with the number of overlapping show/toggle requests issued before the first terminal lookup or launch resolves; each request can independently launch another terminal.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: duplicate subprocess launches, extra retained terminal/rendering resources, and higher latency/CPU during slow local or remote terminal startup
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this chat-window terminal path, there was no per-window show operation that could independently launch a terminal for the same window. A single user request launched at most the requested terminal.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every call to show() observes the shared terminal set before awaiting getChatWindowTerminal(), but no pending promise is recorded. Concurrent calls therefore all see an empty set and independently cross the terminal-creation boundary.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 144 invokes `getChatWindowTerminal` independently from each `show()` after an empty-set check, with no per-window pending operation recorded around the await.
Findings.Title: Coalesce terminal show operations per chat window
Findings.Impact: Rapidly clicking the terminal toggle, or clicking it while restoration is still populating the window, can start two or more terminals for one chat window—especially when remote/profile initialization makes the first launch slow—wasting subprocess, CPU, and memory resources.
Findings.Evidence: show() checks `!terminals.size` and then awaits `_source.getChatWindowTerminal(...)` at the changed line without an in-flight guard. `toggle()` calls show while `terminalsVisible` remains false until an editor arrives. The source reaches `SessionsTerminalContribution._ensureTerminal`, whose empty result path calls `_createTerminalForSession`/`ITerminalService.createTerminal`; parallel callers can all pass the empty checks before any created terminal is tracked. Existing generation checks only cancel hide/close races and do not coalesce shows.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep one in-flight show promise per window and have subsequent show/toggle requests join it; preserve the existing generation cancellation so a hide or close during the shared launch still releases the resulting terminal exactly once.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reveal a chat in its own window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command awaits content resolution, auxiliary-window creation, scoped services/parts, chat/editor restoration, and the first layout before returning. Chat-model holding avoids reloading an already loaded transcript while the view moves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One creation per distinct newly opened chat; zero for an already open chat, with same-chat pending opens coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision had no generic part-based chat-window service on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Window creation must complete before parts and editors can be attached, so it is on the open command's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct chats opened concurrently and number of editors/created parts restored into each window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests for the same chat are coalesced by `InFlightOperations`; an already open resolved chat is revealed. Different chats can open concurrently and have no global limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Open windows act as a positive cache and same-chat pending opens are coalesced. Failed/unknown content is not negatively cached, which is appropriate for explicit user retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete open path and same-key in-flight map are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Auxiliary-window creation duration and typical editor counts vary, but the cardinality and coalescing behavior are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: expensive creation is one per requested distinct window and duplicate same-chat opens are coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore chat windows after workbench startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Restoration runs asynchronously after the provider and restore setting become ready, so it does not block the main workbench restore, but each restored chat window waits for `canRestore` and auxiliary-window opening before the next stored entry. Terminal population is scheduled separately after each window appears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write serialized restoration state through the workspace storage service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read when restoration starts plus save/remove events; payload grows with restored windows, groups, and serializable editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No part-based chat-window restoration state was handled by this service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial JSON read is on the restoration path but not the main startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create one auxiliary window for each restorable stored chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per effective stored chat that `canRestore` accepts; the loop serializes these calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic restoration path and its auxiliary-window calls are added by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each creation delays that restored window and all later entries, but remains off the main workbench critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or acquire a session terminal for every restored window whose terminal part was stored as shown
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one initial terminal operation per restored terminal-visible window; operations can overlap across windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base path did not repopulate terminals in part-based chat windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the main startup critical path, but concurrent launches contend with post-startup rendering and make restored windows fully usable later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of persisted chat windows, serialized editors/created parts per window, and the subset with terminals shown.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Chat-window validation/opening is serialized by the restore loop. Restored terminal shows are independently scheduled and can overlap across windows; no shared terminal-launch limiter was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stored state is retained while restore is disabled/pending and removed after restoration; `canRestore` relies on loaded session state. Existing/pending chat opens are deduplicated by chat key. Terminal shows lack per-window in-flight coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for sequencing and boundary cardinality; moderate for aggregate startup contention because user window counts vary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical persisted-window counts are unknown and the feature is disabled by default; session loading can wait up to the provider's 30-second timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: The broad restoration fan-out is bounded by stored windows and opening is serialized. The independently scheduled terminal launch path contributes to the separately reported missing-coalescing risk when another show overlaps.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle or restore terminals in a chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Showing terminals awaits session cwd/profile resolution, terminal acquisition or creation, moving the terminal editor into the window part, and optional focus. Hiding moves running terminals back to the panel without killing them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the user home directory when the session has no known cwd
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per show attempt that lacks session cwd, including overlapping attempts; normal sessions with cwd avoid it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This fallback was not invoked by a chat-window terminal show path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before terminal lookup/creation, so it delays showing terminals.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a local or agent-host terminal process and renderer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Intended as one initial terminal per window, but overlapping shows can each launch one before either is tracked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No chat-window show operation could race terminal creation for the same window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launch is awaited by each show and dominates slow local/remote startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of overlapping clicks/restoration-triggered shows before the first terminal launch resolves; remote/profile startup increases the overlap window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: There is no per-window pending-show promise. Multiple `show`/`toggle` calls can execute concurrently while visibility remains false, and each can independently reach terminal creation. Different windows are also unrestricted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Running terminals are retained per window and reused after hide/show, with disposed entries removed. There is no cache/coalescing state for a pending first terminal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: all callers inspect an empty shared set before an unguarded await and the source creates when no tracked terminal exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap frequency depends on user interaction and terminal launch latency, but slow remote starts make duplicate requests realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing regression: overlapping requests can create duplicate subprocesses for one window.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a chat window with terminals visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every native window layout synchronously lays out the part grid and active editor panes. With terminals visible, the changed code captures terminal height, performs the full grid layout, then performs an unconditional `resizeCell` relayout to restore height.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Propagate changed terminal rows/columns/pixel dimensions to the terminal process manager
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the terminal resize debouncer's effective rate; duplicate layouts reevaluate dimensions twice and may collapse to one final process update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Terminal dimension propagation already existed, but the diff's chat-window grid invokes terminal/editor layout an extra time per resize.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous grid/xterm evaluation is on the resize critical path; eventual process resize work follows.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Window resize event frequency and number/complexity of visible part cells and active editor panes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the renderer event path; resize events are sequential but can arrive at frame rate. Terminal PTY dimension updates use their existing debouncer, while grid/editor/xterm layout CPU still runs synchronously.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No layout-result cache is used. The existing `_update` path compares heights before corrective resizing, but the resize path does not.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: `grid.layout` is immediately followed by `resizeCell`, and SplitView.resizeView unconditionally relayouts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame loss varies by hardware and pane contents; the duplicate synchronous relayout is guaranteed for width-only resizes with a visible terminal.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI regression: the added unconditional corrective resize doubles layout work in cases where terminal height did not change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag editors or cards to create, move, or merge part-grid cells
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drag start captures cell/card rectangles and overlay state. Retargeting performs an in-memory serialized-grid dry run only when the drop zone changes, then updates transform/clip-based reflow visuals; drop commits once.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible grid cells, registered native overlays, and distinct drop-zone transitions during one drag.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer interaction; hysteresis and candidate-key checks suppress repeated previews while remaining in the same zone.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The reflow object caches shown rectangles for the drag lifetime and is disposed/reset after settle or cancellation. Overlay registrations are disposed with their hosts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for synchronous geometry/grid-copy work and suppression behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large custom part counts could make geometry scans noticeable, but realistic chat-window grids are small and previews are not run on every pointer event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: changed-zone gating, transform-based motion, cleanup, and small effective grid cardinality bound the interaction work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close a chat window or move its chat back to the main window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Closing first releases terminal ownership, closes parts, disposes per-window services/listeners/maps, and closes the auxiliary window. Moving back serializes main-part editor identities, closes the window, waits for the main session/editor restore, then reopens those editors.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close/focus the auxiliary window and return editor state to the main window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One auxiliary-window close per chat window; editor reopening is batched through `openEditors`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic part-based chat-window lifecycle did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the explicit move-to-main command's critical path; ordinary unload cleanup is shutdown work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of editor groups/editors and terminals owned by the closing window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One close per window is guarded by closed/closing state. Same-chat reopen is coalesced by the chat-window open service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Window, grid, host, overlay, terminal, and session maps all have explicit removal/disposal paths; terminal instances are intentionally retained by their session after hiding/closing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cleanup ownership and batching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor close confirmation and restore duration depend on editor types, but no unbounded retained collection was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: lifecycle cleanup is explicit and editor reopening is grouped rather than per-editor IPC.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 296-file inventory, focusing changed startup/restoration, auxiliary-window, part-grid/rendering, terminal subprocess, and long-lived lifecycle paths. Reported two high-confidence regressions: missing coalescing can duplicate terminal subprocess launches, and terminal-visible resizing performs an unconditional second full grid relayout. Other boundary fan-out, caches, drag work, and cleanup paths were bounded or intentionally off the main critical path.
